Repeat Criteria
Tags: courses
Short Description: The criteria specifying how many times a course may be taken, the maximum credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment, and any restrictions on repeating the course within the same term.
Repeat Criteria
The criteria specifying the limits and conditions for repeating a course, including:
Maximum Enrollments: The maximum number of times a course may be taken.
Maximum Credits Allowed: The maximum number of credits that may be earned through repeated enrollment during a student’s academic career.
Same-Term Repeats: Whether the course may be repeated within the same term.
Maximum Credits Allowed Per Term: The maximum number of credits that may be taken through repeat enrollment in a single term.

Credential Type
Tags: programs
Short Description: Identifies the type of academic credential awarded for a program. (Degree, Major, Minor, Certificate)
Credential Type

The degree is the academic credential awarded by the University upon successful completion of an approved program of study and its associated requirements. Degrees may include bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees.
The major is the primary field of study within a degree program, consisting of a defined set of courses and requirements that students must complete.
University Manual 8.20.40 Major Fields of Study. An undergraduate student’s concentrated field of study in a degree-granting college shall be the student’s “major”; Fannon Institute students may have a “preferred major.” The major field of study for graduate students shall be the student’s “program.”

Undergraduate programs are required to have a minimum or 120 credits, and a maximum of 148 (UM 8.21.10)
Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)
In Kuali, the term program refers to all credential types; Degrees, majors, minors, and certificates. In the Manual, program refers to a graduate student’s major field of study.

A secondary concentration of undergraduate courses that provides students with a defined area of study outside their major. A minor generally requires 18 or more credits and is listed on the student’s permanent academic record after graduation.
University Manual 8.20.50 Minor Fields of Study. Undergraduate Students may declare a “minor” field of study. A minor is a secondary concentration of courses.

18 or more credits of related studies offered by one or more departments or programs and sponsored by a faculty member. (UM 8.20.50)
At least 12 credits at the 200-level or above ( UM 8.20.51)
At least 8 credits must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.51)
Minimum GPA average of 2.0 must be earned in the minor’s required courses (UM 8.20.51)
A maximum of two courses can apply to both the major and minor field of study (UM 8.20.52)
An approved course of study designed to further knowledge in a field of interest, provide specialized training, and/or enhance professional skills.

Undergraduate certificates generally require 15-21 credits of coursework (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificates are available to degree seeking and certificate-only seeking undergraduate students (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificate courses may not be pass/fail (UM 8.20.71)
Graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 16 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)
Post-master’s graduate certificates require 12 credits minimum, 18 credits maximum. (GSM Appendix J.1.1)

S/U Only
Tags: courses
Short Description: A grading method in which student performance is recorded as S (Satisfactory) or U (Unsatisfactory) rather than a letter grade.
S/U Only

Certain courses do not lend themselves to precise grading. For these courses, only S (satisfactory) or U (unsatisfactory) is given to all students enrolled. S/U courses are labeled as such in the course descriptions in this catalog. S/U courses are not counted as courses taken under the Pass-Fail option.
D1 is the only General Education outcome that can be graded using S/U or Letter Grades. All other outcomes must be graded by Letter Grades.

General Education Outcomes
Tags: courses
Short Description: Undergraduate students must complete at least 3 credits addressing each of the 12 General Education Student Learning Outcomes, organized across four areas: Knowledge, Competencies, Responsibilities, and Integrate & Apply.
General Education Outcomes

The General Education program will assess student exposure to twelve Student Learning Outcomes in four areas:
A. Build knowledge of diverse peoples and cultures and of the natural and physical world.
(A1) STEM Disciplines (A2) Social & Behavioral Sciences (A3) Humanities (A4) Art & Design
B. Develop intellectual and interdisciplinary competencies for academic and lifelong learning.
(B1) Write Effectively (B2) Communicate Effectively (B3) Mathematical, Statistical, or Computational Strategies (B4) Information Literacy
C. Exercise individual and social responsibilities.
(C1) Civic Knowledge & Responsibilies (C2) Global Responsibility (C3) Diversity & Inclusion
D. Integrate and apply these abilities and capacities, adapting them to new settings, questions, and responsibilities to lay the foundation for lifelong learning.
(D1) Integrate & Apply

General Education courses may assess one or two Student Learning Outcomes in the following configurations:
Knowledge (A) and Competency (B)
Knowledge (A) and Responsibility (C)
Competency (B) and Competency (B)
Competency (B) and Responsibility (C)
Integration (D) and Competency (B)
Integration (D) and Responsibility (C)
